Hi Alyssa / Rob,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear signals on latency sensitivity and peak throughput patterns. Quick recap from our side and the asks we left with: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: patient-facing triage responses must return within tight latency bounds; current prototype hits 300–500ms p95 on the 13B model and spikes under concurrency.
- Business goal: 95th percentile < 200ms for single-turn triage prompts (average prompt length ~ 80 tokens); 99th < 400ms for multi-turn flows if possible.
- Throughput pattern: predictable daytime spikes (~1200 rps for 10–15 minutes), steady baseline ~150–200 rps.
- Data control: logs must be archived for 6 months; PHI concerns require VPC or on-prem option for any live patient data.

Key technical constraints we captured
- Model candidates: your team is evaluating Llama-2-70B quantized vs a fine-tuned 13B variant for hallucination control.
- Average input length: 60–100 tokens; worst-case sequences ~1024 tokens in rare diagnostic flows.
- KV cache reuse expected for follow-up clarifying turns; cold-start latency matters.
- Network: you prefer regional isolation for EU/US traffic and strict egress controls.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) I'll share a short SLO worksheet that maps your p95/p99 targets to topology options and cost estimates (attached). -> action: jonas to share worksheet (attached).
2) Please introduce your infra lead (Rob) so we can validate network/egress constraints and discuss VPC/private deployment feasibility. -> action: alyssa to introduce.
3) Schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with Marissa (ops) and Sean (runtime) to run through quantization, batching, and topology tradeoffs. Proposed window: Thu-Fri next week. -> action: marissa to propose times.

Attachments: healthtech-slo-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet mapping SLOs to topo/cost scenarios).

Thanks — I'll follow up with a proposed agenda for the deep-dive.

Best,

Rob / Alyssa — thanks for the intro, Rob. As promised, a concise view of topology options keyed to your SLOs and the tradeoffs we discussed. I've attached a short PDF with diagrams and a benchmark CSV; summarized below.

High-level options (tradeoff summary)
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted)
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value, we handle autoscaling and fallback routing; shared infra costs.
   - Cons: higher egress surface for PHI unless combined with token-level redaction; we can enable private networking tunnels for select customers but need to scope.
   - Latency profile: p95 for 13B quantized ~ 120–200ms (depending on batching & sequence length); p99 ~ 260–420ms.

2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in customer region)
   - Pros: predictable throughput for daytime spikes, strict network controls, dedicated GPUs reduce tail variance.
   - Cons: longer onboarding (provisioning GPUs), commit-based pricing.
   - Latency profile: p95 ~ 80–180ms for 13B optimized kernels; with 70B quantized p95 ~ 150–240ms.

3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Pros: full control (KMS/HSM, private control plane), best for PHI/regulatory constraints.
   - Cons: ops overhead for your team or our on-prem package; baseline cost higher but latency predictable.

Performance levers we recommend for your workload
- Aggressive KV caching for multi-turn flows (reduces token compute for clarifying prompts).
- Sequence-length aware batching windows: prefer smaller, latency-aware batches during daytime spikes.
- Mixed-precision + 4-bit quantization for 70B experiments; maintain 13B as fallback for low-latency endpoints.
- Warm pool of GPUs (pre-warmed KV cache) during expected peak windows to avoid cold-start spikes.

Initial configuration proposal for the deep-dive
- Run staged load test (we'll provide a driver) against a sandbox in your us-west2 VPC: 1) baseline small-concurrency, 2) 15-minute spike test (1200 rps), 3) multi-turn flows with KV reuse.
- Instrumentation: token-level latency breakdown (kernel time, queueing, network), tracing hooks to link requests to Redwood Console.
- Goals for the session: map SLOs to one recommended topology + a fallback plan (model variant routing).

Attachments: redwood-inference-topology-options.pdf, latency-benchmark-matrix.csv

I'll propose a 60-minute slot for Fri 11:00–12:00 PST; Marissa will send a calendar invite. If you'd prefer Thu afternoon, please flag.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
